preconditions.description: The input list must contain exactly two elements.

preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(color, str) for color in colors)
preconditions.description: Both elements in the list must be strings.

postconditions.description: The function must return one of the specified color outcomes.
If both bears are black, the offspring will be black.
If both bears are brown, the offspring will be brown.
If both bears are white, the offspring will be white.

postconditions.expression: (colors[0] == 'black' and colors[1] == 'brown') or (colors[0] == 'brown' and colors[1] == 'black') -> return_value == 'dark brown'
postconditions.description: If one bear is black and the other is brown, the offspring will be dark brown.

postconditions.expression: (colors[0] == 'black' and colors[1] == 'white') or (colors[0] == 'white' and colors[1] == 'black') -> return_value == 'grey'
postconditions.description: If one bear is black and the other is white, the offspring will be grey.

postconditions.expression: (colors[0] == 'brown' and colors[1] == 'white') or (colors[0] == 'white' and colors[1] == 'brown') -> return_value == 'light brown'
postconditions.description: If one bear is brown and the other is white, the offspring will be light brown.

postconditions.expression: not any(color in {'black', 'brown', 'white'} for color in colors) -> return_value == 'unknown'
postconditions.description: If either bear is not black, brown, or white, the offspring color is unknown.
